memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia, psoriasis, and hypertension.
Patient reports mild urinary frequency, occasional nocturia, and stable psoriasis plaques on elbows and knees. Blood pressure measured 142/88 mmHg, pulse 78, BMI 27. Prostate exam shows mildly enlarged, smooth gland. Skin exam reveals well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale. Smoking status: never smoked. Pack-years: 0.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
PSA: 4.2 ng/mL (ref 0-4.0) – slightly elevated.
Urine routine: pH 6.0, negative for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, blood; few squamous cells.
Ultrasound KUB: Prostate volume 28 mL, post‑void residual 25 mL; no hydronephrosis.
Liver function: ALT 32 U/L (ref ≤40), AST 28 U/L (ref ≤35), ALP 78 U/L (ref 40‑129), GGT 45 U/L (ref ≤51), total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL (ref 0.2‑1.2).
CBC: Hb 13.8 g/dL (ref 13.0‑17.0), WBC 6.2×10⁹/L (ref 4.0‑10.0), platelets 210×10⁹/L (ref 150‑400).
Serum creatinine: 0.96 mg/dL (ref 0.6‑1.2); eGFR 78 mL/min/1.73m² (ref >60).
Serum potassium: 4.3 mmol/L (ref 3.5‑5.0).

memories.author: D05
memories.text: ECG: Sinus rhythm, rate 72 bpm. No ST‑T changes. Left ventricular voltage within normal limits. No evidence of prior infarction.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been noticing I need to get up twice at night to pass urine, and my skin patches are itchy but not worsening. My BP feels okay; I take my tablets as prescribed.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia, psoriasis, hypertension.
Patient reports nocturia reduced to once nightly, mild improvement in psoriasis itch after topical steroids. Blood pressure 138/84 mmHg. No new symptoms. Prostate exam unchanged. Skin plaques less erythematous. Smoking status: never smoked. Pack-years: 0.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Referral to Dermatology, Dr. Priya Rao, for refractory psoriasis plaques despite topical therapy, to consider systemic agent or phototherapy.

CBC: Hb 13.9 g/dL (ref 13.0‑17.0), WBC 6.0×10⁹/L (ref 4.0‑10.0), platelets 208×10⁹/L (ref 150‑400).
Serum creatinine: 0.97 mg/dL (ref 0.6‑1.2); eGFR 77 mL/min/1.73m².

PSA: 4.0 ng/mL (ref 0‑4.0) – at upper limit of normal.

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dermatology review: Plaques mild‑moderate, PASI 6. Recommended narrow‑band UVB phototherapy twice weekly; continue current topicals. No need for systemic methotrexate dose increase at this time.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Benign prostatic hyperplasia, psoriasis, hypertension.
Patient reports occasional urgency but no incontinence; psoriasis plaques stable on phototherapy. Blood pressure 150/92 mmHg, slight rise. Prostate exam: mildly enlarged, no nodules. Skin: plaques thinner, less scale. Smoking status: never smoked. Pack-years: 0.
